attributes.name: applicable_legal_framework
attributes.description: The primary legal or regulatory framework under which this co-employment risk assessment is conducted. Determines which risk factors, thresholds, and mitigation standards apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dol_joint_employer|nlrb_browning_ferris|flsa_joint_employment|state_specific|irs_worker_classification|multiple — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791); NLRB Browning-Ferris Industries Decision (2015); FLSA (29 U.S.C. § 203); IRS Rev. Rul. 87-41

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the co-employment risk assessment was formally approved by the designated approver. Null if not yet approved. Used for compliance tracking and audit trail.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Recordkeeping Requirements

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the co-employment risk assessment was formally conducted. Principal business event date for this transaction record. Used for scheduling reassessments and tracking compliance cadence.
attributes.references: DOL Joint Employer Rule; ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: assessment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the assessor to document qualitative observations, contextual factors, client-specific circumstances, and any additional risk considerations not captured by the structured scoring fields.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail

attributes.name: assessment_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the co-employment risk assessment, used in legal correspondence, audit trails, and compliance reporting. Format: COE-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}.
attributes.references: ASA Best Practices for Co-Employment Risk Management; DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: assessment_state
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state code where the client engagement and worker placement is located. Determines which state-specific joint employer statutes, co-employment laws, and worker classification tests apply in addition to federal standards.
attributes.references: State Joint Employer Statutes; CCPA (California); SHRM State Employment Law Compliance

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the co-employment risk assessment workflow. Tracks progression from initial draft through legal review, approval, and eventual closure or reassessment scheduling.
attributes.references: ASA Best Practices for Co-Employment Risk Management; SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: assignment_duration_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) reflecting the length of the worker's assignment at the client site. Extended assignments (typically 12+ months) increase co-employment and temp-to-perm conversion risk, and may trigger state-specific joint employer protections.
attributes.references: DOL Joint Employer Rule; ASA Staffing Law Compliance Guide; State Joint Employer Statutes

attributes.name: composite_risk_score
attributes.description: Aggregated numeric risk score derived from all individual risk factor scores (supervision, equipment, integration, duration, work method control, disciplinary authority, pay rate setting). Used to determine the overall risk rating. Stored as a raw computed value for audit and trend analysis.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: contract_language_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether updated or additional co-employment protective contract language is required in the Master Service Agreement (MSA) or Statement of Work (SOW) as a mitigation action for identified risks. Triggers contract review workflow in DocuSign CLM.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DocuSign CLM; MSA Best Practices

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this co-employment risk assessment record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and compliance record retention per DOL and IRS requirements.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; DOL Recordkeeping Requirements (29 CFR Part 516)

attributes.name: disciplinary_authority_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) assessing whether the client exercises disciplinary authority over the placed worker, including the ability to terminate, discipline, or reassign the worker. Client disciplinary authority is a key factor in NLRB joint employer determinations.
attributes.references: NLRB Browning-Ferris Industries Decision (2015); DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: engagement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the client engagement type being assessed: temporary staffing, contract placement, Statement of Work (SOW), managed service, or Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO). Drives which risk factors and legal frameworks apply.
attributes.references: ASA Staffing Law Compliance Guide; DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: equipment_provision_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) evaluating whether the client provides tools, equipment, workspace, or materials to the placed worker. Client-provided equipment is a significant indicator of employment relationship and co-employment risk under IRS and DOL worker classification tests.
attributes.references: IRS Worker Classification Rules (Rev. Rul. 87-41); DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: incident_history_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this client account has a prior history of co-employment claims, NLRB charges, DOL investigations, or joint employer litigation. Prior incident history is a significant risk escalation factor.
attributes.references: NLRB Browning-Ferris Framework; DOL Joint Employer Rule; ASA Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: insurance_rider_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a co-employment insurance rider or endorsement is required on the staffing firm's liability policy for this client engagement. Triggered by high or critical risk ratings to protect against joint employer liability claims.
attributes.references: ASA Risk Management Guidelines; Workers Compensation Insurance Standards; NAPEO Best Practices

attributes.name: legal_counsel_name
attributes.description: Name of the attorney or law firm that conducted the legal review of this co-employment risk assessment. Confidential business information used for accountability and legal privilege tracking.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; Attorney-Client Privilege Standards

attributes.name: legal_counsel_opinion
attributes.description: Formal opinion rendered by legal counsel following review of the co-employment risk assessment. Drives final disposition of the engagement and required mitigation actions. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege considerations.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; Attorney-Client Privilege Standards

attributes.name: legal_counsel_review_date
attributes.description: Date on which legal counsel completed their review of this co-employment risk assessment. Null if review has not yet been completed. Used for compliance tracking and audit trail.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Recordkeeping Requirements

attributes.name: legal_counsel_review_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this co-employment risk assessment requires formal review by internal or external legal counsel before the engagement proceeds or continues. Typically triggered by high or critical risk ratings.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule; NLRB Browning-Ferris Framework

attributes.name: legal_counsel_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the legal counsel review process for this co-employment risk assessment. Tracks whether legal review has been initiated, is in progress, completed, or escalated to outside counsel.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; SOC 2 Type II Audit Trail

attributes.name: mitigation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing detailed recommended mitigation actions, corrective measures, and risk reduction strategies identified during the assessment. Supplements the structured mitigation flags with qualitative guidance for compliance officers and account managers.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule

attributes.name: msa_coe_clause_present
attributes.business_glossary_term: Master Service Agreement (MSA) Co-Employment Clause Present Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the client's Master Service Agreement (MSA) contains co-employment protective language and indemnification clauses. Absence of MSA co-employment clauses is a significant risk factor requiring immediate contract remediation.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DocuSign CLM; MSA Best Practices

attributes.name: pay_rate_setting_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) evaluating whether the client influences or sets the worker's pay rate, bill rate, or compensation structure. Client involvement in pay rate determination is a significant co-employment risk indicator under DOL and IRS worker classification standards.
attributes.references: IRS Worker Classification Rules (Rev. Rul. 87-41); DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: reassessment_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date by which this co-employment risk assessment must be reviewed and updated. Typically set based on risk rating (e.g., critical: 90 days, high: 180 days, medium: 12 months, low: 24 months) or triggered by material changes in the engagement.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule

attributes.name: reassessment_trigger
attributes.description: The reason or event that triggered this co-employment risk assessment. Distinguishes between routine scheduled assessments and those triggered by material changes such as assignment extensions, scope changes, regulatory updates, or co-employment incidents. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: scheduled|assignment_extension|scope_change|client_request|regulatory_change|incident|risk_escalation — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall co-employment and joint employment risk rating derived from the composite risk score and qualitative assessment. Drives escalation protocols, mitigation actions, and legal counsel review requirements. Critical rating triggers immediate legal review and potential engagement restructuring.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; DOL Joint Employer Rule; NLRB Browning-Ferris Framework

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this co-employment risk assessment originated or was imported. Supports data lineage tracking across the lakehouse silver layer. Bullhorn ATS/CRM is the primary source for client and placement context.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II Data Lineage Requirements; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

attributes.name: supervision_level_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) evaluating the degree to which the client directly supervises, directs, and controls the day-to-day work activities of the placed worker. High scores indicate greater client control, elevating co-employment risk. Key factor in DOL joint employer and NLRB Browning-Ferris tests.
attributes.references: DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791); NLRB Browning-Ferris Industries Decision (2015)

attributes.name: supervisor_training_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether client supervisor training on co-employment boundaries is required as a mitigation action. Training covers prohibited supervisory behaviors, proper work direction protocols, and co-employment liability avoidance.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; EEOC Compliance Training Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this co-employment risk assessment record. Supports audit trail integrity and change tracking per SOC 2 and DOL recordkeeping standards.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; DOL Recordkeeping Requirements (29 CFR Part 516)

attributes.name: work_method_control_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) evaluating the extent to which the client dictates how work is performed (methods, processes, procedures) rather than only specifying the desired outcome. Client control over work methods is a primary indicator of employment relationship under IRS and DOL tests.
attributes.references: IRS Worker Classification Rules (Rev. Rul. 87-41); FLSA Joint Employment Guidance (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: worker_classification_type
attributes.description: The tax and employment classification of the worker(s) in the assessed engagement: W-2 employee, 1099 Independent Contractor (IC), Corp-to-Corp, or Employer of Record (EOR). Classification type significantly affects co-employment risk profile and applicable legal frameworks.
attributes.references: IRS Worker Classification Rules (Rev. Rul. 87-41); FLSA; IRS Form 1099; IRS Form W-2

attributes.name: worker_communication_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether specific worker communication protocols are required as a mitigation action, such as written notices to workers clarifying the employment relationship, reporting structure, and the staffing firm's role as the employer of record.
attributes.references: ASA Co-Employment Risk Management Guidelines; NLRB Browning-Ferris Framework; FLSA

attributes.name: workforce_integration_score
attributes.description: Numeric risk score (1–5) assessing the degree to which the placed worker is integrated into the client's regular workforce operations, including participation in client meetings, use of client systems, client email, and client org chart inclusion. High integration elevates co-employment risk.
attributes.references: NLRB Browning-Ferris Industries Decision (2015); DOL Joint Employer Rule (29 CFR Part 791)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this placement compliance check record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for record origination and supports SOC 2 Type II audit logging requirements.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5; CCPA

attributes.name: credential_verification_status
attributes.description: Status of required professional credential and license verification for this placement. Applies to placements requiring specific certifications (e.g., nursing licenses, CDL, OSHA certifications, IT certifications). Verified through Sterling Background Check and internal credentialing processes.
attributes.references: Sterling Background Check; OSHA; ASA Best Practices; client MSA requirements

attributes.name: drug_screen_date
attributes.description: The date on which the drug screen specimen was collected and/or the final result was reported. Used to validate that drug screening was completed within the required pre-placement window.
attributes.references: DOL; OSHA; Sterling Background Check

attributes.name: drug_screen_status
attributes.description: Status of the pre-placement drug screening for this worker. 'negative' clears the worker for placement. 'positive' blocks placement and may trigger adverse action. 'not_required' applies when client or placement type does not mandate drug screening. Managed through Sterling Background Check.
attributes.references: DOL; OSHA; Sterling Background Check; ASA Best Practices; client MSA requirements

attributes.name: eeoc_self_id_collected
attributes.business_glossary_term: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) Self-Identification Collected Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the EEOC voluntary self-identification form (race, ethnicity, gender, disability, veteran status) has been collected from the worker for this placement. Required for EEOC and OFCCP reporting compliance for federal contractor clients.
attributes.references: EEOC; OFCCP; 41 CFR Part 60; ASA Best Practices

attributes.name: noncompete_nda_check_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Non-Compete and NDA Conflict Check Status
attributes.description: Status of the review for existing non-compete agreements and NDAs that could restrict the worker's placement with the target client. 'conflict_identified' requires legal review before placement proceeds. Tracked via DocuSign CLM.
attributes.references: DocuSign CLM; ASA Best Practices; SHRM

attributes.name: ofccp_applicability_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) Applicability Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this placement is subject to OFCCP affirmative action and equal employment opportunity requirements because the client is a federal contractor or subcontractor. Drives additional compliance obligations including AAP tracking and adverse impact analysis.
attributes.references: OFCCP; 41 CFR Part 60; Executive Order 11246

attributes.name: onboarding_status
attributes.description: Status of the worker onboarding process in SAP SuccessFactors, including completion of required forms, policy acknowledgments, direct deposit setup, and benefits enrollment. 'complete' is required before a placement can generate billable hours.
attributes.references: SAP SuccessFactors; DOL; ASA Best Practices

attributes.name: overall_compliance_result
attributes.description: The final aggregated compliance determination for this placement. 'pass' authorizes the placement to go active and generate billable hours. 'fail' blocks activation. 'conditional_pass' indicates clearance granted with documented exceptions or waivers. 'pending_review' indicates escalation to compliance team.
attributes.references: ASA Best Practices; DOL; SOC 2 Type II; OFCCP

attributes.name: placement_type
attributes.description: The type of placement being compliance-checked. Determines which compliance requirements are applicable (e.g., I-9 requirements differ for SOW vs. direct placement; workers comp requirements differ for temporary vs. direct hire). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: temporary|contract_to_hire|direct_placement|per_diem|sow|rpo — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ASA Best Practices; IRS Worker Classification Rules; FLSA

attributes.name: safety_training_date
attributes.description: The date on which all required safety training modules were completed by the worker in the LMS. Used to validate training currency and identify workers requiring refresher training.
attributes.references: OSHA; SAP SuccessFactors LMS

attributes.name: safety_training_status
attributes.description: Status of required OSHA and client-specific safety training completion for this placement. 'complete' indicates all mandatory safety modules have been passed in the LMS (SAP SuccessFactors). Required for placements in industrial, construction, healthcare, and other regulated environments.
attributes.references: OSHA; SAP SuccessFactors LMS; ASA Best Practices; client MSA requirements

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this compliance check record originated or was primarily managed. Supports data lineage tracking in the Silver layer lakehouse and cross-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this placement compliance check record was most recently modified. Tracks the latest state change for audit trail purposes and supports incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer

attributes.name: waiver_authorization
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized approver who granted a compliance waiver for this placement (if applicable). Required when check_status = 'waived' or overall_compliance_result = 'conditional_pass'. Provides audit trail for waiver accountability.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; DOL Audit Requirements; ASA Best Practices

attributes.name: waiver_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which a granted compliance waiver expires. After this date, the outstanding compliance item must be completed or the placement may be suspended. Drives automated compliance expiry alerts.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; DOL Audit Requirements; ASA Best Practices

attributes.name: waiver_reason
attributes.description: Documented business justification for any compliance waiver granted for this placement. Required for audit trail integrity. Examples include client-approved exceptions, emergency placements with post-start completion commitments, or regulatory exemptions.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; DOL Audit Requirements; FCRA

attributes.name: workers_comp_code
attributes.description: The NCCI workers compensation classification code assigned to this placement based on the job duties and work environment. Drives workers comp premium calculation in TempWorks Payroll and ensures correct coverage is in place before assignment start.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Classification; DOL; TempWorks Payroll; OSHA

products.name: workers_comp_policy
products.description: Master record for workers' compensation insurance policies and associated claims covering contingent workers across states. Policy header captures policy number, insurance carrier, policy period, covered states, experience modification rate (EMR), NCCI class codes by job type, premium amounts, and policy renewal dates. Claim detail records capture claim number, incident date, filing date, injury description, claim type (medical only, lost time, permanent partial disability), claim status (open, reserved, closed, reopened), total incurred cost, reserve amount, adjuster, litigation flag, subrogation flag, and settlement date. Links to osha_incident for workplace injury correlation. SSOT for all workers' compensation policy and claim data. Managed through TempWorks Payroll integration. Supports OSHA incident linkage, state-mandated workers' comp compliance, experience mod management, and insurance cost optimization.

attributes.name: workers_comp_policy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the workers compensation policy record. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: MASTER_AGREEMENT — represents a long-running insurance policy binding the staffing firm to coverage obligations across states and worker populations.
attributes.references: TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: contract_msa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.msa. Business justification: MSAs specify workers' comp coverage requirements, carrier ratings, and certificate of insurance obligations. Real business need: MSA insurance compliance for client certificate delivery and audit.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: osha_incident_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Incident ID
attributes.description: Reference to the linked OSHA incident record when a workers comp claim is associated with a workplace injury event. Supports OSHA incident-to-claim correlation for regulatory reporting and safety analytics.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: premium_allocation_cost_center_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Premium Allocation Cost Center Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Workers comp premiums are allocated to cost centers based on headcount, payroll, or claims experience for departmental cost tracking and budget management. Staffing firms allocate insurance costs to o
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: premium_expense_gl_account_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Premium Expense Gl Account Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Workers compensation insurance premiums are expensed to specific GL accounts (typically 'Insurance Expense - Workers Comp') for financial reporting. Monthly premium accruals and annual true-ups requir
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: regulatory_violation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_violation. Business justification: When a workers compensation policy issue (e.g., coverage lapse, misclassification, premium fraud) results in a regulatory violation, this FK links to the regulatory_violation record. Clear 1:N relatio
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: supplier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to vendor.supplier. Business justification: Workers' comp policies are issued by insurance carriers (suppliers in vendor management context). Track supplier for claims management, premium reconciliation, carrier performance assessment, and vend
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: adjuster_name
attributes.description: Full name of the insurance carrier's claims adjuster assigned to manage this workers compensation claim. Primary point of contact for claim status updates, reserve changes, and settlement negotiations.
attributes.references: TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: adjuster_phone
attributes.description: Direct phone number for the claims adjuster assigned to this workers compensation claim. Used for claim status inquiries and coordination of return-to-work activities.
attributes.references: TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: aggregate_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum total dollar amount the carrier will pay for all claims under this policy during the policy period. Null indicates unlimited aggregate coverage. Critical for risk exposure assessment and reinsurance planning.
attributes.references: State Workers Compensation Statutes; American Staffing Association (ASA)

attributes.name: annual_premium_amount
attributes.description: Total annual premium amount in USD payable to the insurance carrier for this policy period. Calculated as the sum of (payroll per $100 × class code rate × EMR) across all covered class codes and states. Used for financial planning, burden rate calculation, and cost allocation.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; Oracle NetSuite ERP — Accounts Payable

attributes.name: audited_payroll_amount
attributes.description: Actual total payroll in USD for all covered workers as determined by the annual policy audit. Differences between estimated and audited payroll result in premium adjustments (additional premium or return premium). Populated post-audit.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

attributes.name: body_part_code
attributes.description: Standardized NCCI body part code identifying the anatomical location of the workplace injury (e.g., 10=Head, 30=Back, 50=Lower Extremities). Used for claim classification, trend analysis, and safety program targeting.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan — Body Part Codes

attributes.name: carrier_naic_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Carrier Code
attributes.description: Five-digit NAIC company code uniquely identifying the insurance carrier. Used for regulatory filings, state compliance verification, and carrier lookup in state workers compensation databases.
attributes.references: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Company Database

attributes.name: cause_of_injury_code
attributes.description: Standardized NCCI cause of injury code describing how the injury occurred (e.g., 01=Burn, 27=Fall, 83=Strain). Used for claim classification, loss control program development, and OSHA incident analysis.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan — Cause of Injury Codes

attributes.name: claim_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the workers compensation claim was formally filed with the carrier. Used to measure filing timeliness against state-mandated deadlines and carrier SLA requirements.
attributes.references: State Workers Compensation Statutes; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

attributes.name: claim_number
attributes.description: Carrier-assigned claim number for an individual workers compensation claim filed under this policy. Serves as the primary external identifier for claim tracking, adjuster communication, and state reporting. Null for policy header records with no associated claim.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: claim_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the workers compensation claim. Open: active claim under investigation or treatment. Reserved: financial reserve established. Closed: claim resolved with no further activity expected. Reopened: previously closed claim reactivated due to new medical evidence or litigation.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: claim_type
attributes.description: Classification of the workers compensation claim by severity and benefit type. Medical only: no lost work time. Lost time: worker missed work beyond the waiting period. Permanent partial/total disability: lasting impairment. Fatality: death benefit claim. Drives reserve levels and EMR impact. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: medical_only|lost_time|permanent_partial_disability|permanent_total_disability|fatality — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

attributes.name: covered_states
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of two-letter US state codes (e.g., CA,TX,NY) for which this policy provides workers compensation coverage. Determines placement eligibility by state. Each state may have distinct rate schedules and class codes under this policy.
attributes.references: State Workers Compensation Boards; NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this workers compensation policy or claim record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per SOC 2 Type II controls.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Confidentiality)

attributes.name: deductible_amount
attributes.description: Per-claim deductible amount in USD that the staffing firm is responsible for paying before the carrier assumes liability. Applicable for large-deductible policy types. Impacts cash flow planning and claim reserve management.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; American Staffing Association (ASA)

attributes.name: emr
attributes.description: Experience Modification Rate (EMR) assigned by NCCI or applicable state rating bureau. A multiplier applied to the manual premium to reflect the employer's actual loss history relative to industry average. EMR below 1.0 indicates better-than-average safety performance; above 1.0 indicates worse. Critical for premium calculation and client contract eligibility (many clients require EMR ≤ 1.0).
attributes.references: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual; American Staffing Association (ASA)

attributes.name: emr_effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the current EMR value is applicable. EMR is recalculated annually by NCCI or the state rating bureau. Tracking the effective date ensures the correct EMR is applied to premium calculations for each policy period.
attributes.references: NCCI Experience Rating Plan Manual

attributes.name: estimated_annual_payroll
attributes.description: Estimated total payroll in USD for all covered workers during the policy period, used as the basis for initial premium calculation. Reconciled against actual payroll at policy audit. Sourced from TempWorks Payroll payroll projections.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: incident_date
attributes.description: Date on which the workplace injury or occupational illness occurred. The principal real-world event date for the claim. Used for OSHA recordkeeping, state first report of injury filing deadlines, and claim aging analysis.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; State Workers Compensation First Report of Injury Requirements

attributes.name: injury_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the workplace injury or occupational illness, including body part affected, nature of injury, and how the incident occurred. Sourced from the first report of injury and used for OSHA recordkeeping, claim adjudication, and safety trend analysis.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan

attributes.name: litigation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the workers compensation claim has entered litigation (True) or remains in standard adjudication (False). Litigated claims typically have higher total incurred costs and longer closure timelines. Triggers escalation to legal counsel.
attributes.references: American Staffing Association (ASA) Risk Management Guidelines; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: lost_work_days
attributes.description: Total number of calendar days the injured worker was unable to work due to the compensable injury. Used for OSHA 300 log recordkeeping, DART rate calculation, and claim severity benchmarking.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan

attributes.name: ncci_class_codes
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI) Class Codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of NCCI workers compensation class codes applicable under this policy, mapped by job type or occupational category (e.g., 8810 for clerical, 5537 for HVAC). Class codes determine the base rate per $100 of payroll for premium calculation. Managed in TempWorks Payroll workers comp configuration.
attributes.references: NCCI Scopes Manual; TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: paid_indemnity_amount
attributes.description: Total indemnity (wage replacement) benefits paid to date on this claim in USD. Includes temporary total disability (TTD), temporary partial disability (TPD), and permanent disability payments. Tracked separately from medical for benefit analysis.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

attributes.name: paid_medical_amount
attributes.description: Total medical expenses paid to date on this claim in USD, covering physician visits, hospitalization, physical therapy, and prescription costs. Tracked separately from indemnity payments for loss analysis and medical cost management.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: policy_audit_date
attributes.description: Date on which the annual workers compensation policy audit was completed by the carrier. The audit reconciles estimated payroll against actual payroll to determine final premium. Triggers premium adjustment processing.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: policy_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the workers compensation policy coverage begins. Defines the start of the binding coverage period. Workers placed before this date are not covered under this policy.
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL); State Workers Compensation Statutes

attributes.name: policy_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the workers compensation policy coverage ends. Triggers renewal workflows and placement eligibility checks. Null indicates an open-ended or continuously renewed policy.
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL); State Workers Compensation Statutes

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: Externally-assigned policy number issued by the insurance carrier. Used as the primary business identifier for the policy in all carrier communications, audits, and state filings. Maps to the policy number field in TempWorks Payroll workers comp configuration.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll — Workers Compensation Module

attributes.name: policy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the workers compensation policy. Drives eligibility checks for new placements and triggers renewal workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|pending|expired|cancelled|non-renewed|reinstated — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: American Staffing Association (ASA) Risk Management Guidelines; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: policy_type
attributes.description: Classification of the workers compensation policy structure. Determines how premiums are calculated and how losses affect future costs. Guaranteed cost policies have fixed premiums; loss-sensitive and retrospective rating plans adjust based on actual claims experience. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: guaranteed_cost|loss_sensitive|large_deductible|retrospective_rating|captive — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; American Staffing Association (ASA)

attributes.name: premium_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of premium adjustment resulting from the annual payroll audit. Positive value indicates additional premium owed to the carrier; negative value indicates a return premium credit. Feeds into Oracle NetSuite ERP accounts payable or receivable.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; Oracle NetSuite ERP

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for policy renewal negotiation and execution with the carrier. Used to trigger advance renewal workflows, EMR review, and premium renegotiation processes.
attributes.references: American Staffing Association (ASA) Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: Current outstanding reserve amount in USD established by the claims adjuster to cover estimated future claim costs (medical, indemnity, legal). Reserve adequacy directly impacts financial statements and EMR calculations.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; Oracle NetSuite ERP — General Ledger

attributes.name: return_to_work_date
attributes.description: Date on which the injured worker returned to work following a lost-time workers compensation claim. Used to calculate total lost work days, measure return-to-work program effectiveness, and determine indemnity benefit end date.
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL); OSHA 29 CFR Part 1904; American Staffing Association (ASA)

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the workers compensation claim was formally settled and closed. Null for open or reserved claims. Used for claim lifecycle duration analysis and financial close-out processing.
attributes.references: State Workers Compensation Statutes; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this workers compensation policy or claim record was ingested. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation. Primary source is TempWorks Payroll workers compensation module.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: state_claim_number
attributes.description: Claim number assigned by the state workers compensation board or industrial commission for jurisdictional tracking. Distinct from the carrier claim number. Required for state regulatory filings and hearings.
attributes.references: State Workers Compensation Boards; U.S. Department of Labor (DOL)

attributes.name: subrogation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the carrier has identified subrogation potential (True), meaning a third party may be liable for the injury and the carrier may seek recovery of paid losses. Subrogation recovery reduces net claim cost and improves EMR.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; TempWorks Payroll

attributes.name: total_incurred_amount
attributes.description: Total incurred cost of the workers compensation claim in USD, representing the sum of all paid losses plus outstanding reserves. The primary financial measure of claim severity. Used for EMR calculation, loss ratio analysis, and financial reporting.
attributes.references: NCCI Workers Compensation Statistical Plan; Oracle NetSuite ERP

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this workers compensation policy or claim record was last modified in the data platform. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: SOC 2 Type II; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Confidentiality)

products.name: state_compliance_rule
products.description: Reference master for state-specific and local jurisdiction compliance requirements that vary by geography and impact multi-state staffing operations. Captures state/locality, effective date, expiration date, requirement type (ban-the-box, pay transparency, salary history ban, state E-Verify mandate, state-specific drug testing restrictions, portable background check laws, paid sick leave mandate, predictive scheduling, wage theft prevention notice, state mini-WARN Act, independent contractor classification test variations such as ABC test vs. common law test), applicability criteria (employer size threshold, industry sector, worker type), penalty for non-compliance, enforcement agency, and source citation with URL. Drives jurisdiction-aware compliance enforcement for multi-state staffing operations. Distinct from compliance_requirement which owns federal regulations and client-specific contractual mandates.

attributes.name: state_compliance_rule_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the state-specific compliance rule record. Primary key.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard

attributes.name: superseded_by_rule_state_compliance_rule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the state_compliance_rule_id of the newer rule that supersedes this rule. Null if this rule is current and not superseded.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Management Standard

attributes.name: applicability_criteria
attributes.description: Detailed business logic and conditions that determine when this compliance rule must be applied, including employer size, industry, worker type, and other qualifying factors.
attributes.references: State Compliance Implementation Guides

attributes.name: applicable_industry_sector
attributes.description: Industry sector or North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code range to which this rule applies. Null if applies to all industries.
attributes.references: NAICS 2022 Classification System

attributes.name: applicable_worker_type
attributes.description: Type of worker classification to which this compliance rule applies (e.g., all workers, W-2 only, 1099 independent contractors, temporary placements). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: all|W-2|1099|temporary|permanent|contract|direct hire|temp-to-perm — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), IRS Worker Classification Rules

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for internal compliance team notes, implementation guidance, or special considerations for this state rule.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Documentation Standard

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this state compliance rule record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard

attributes.name: documentation_required
attributes.description: Description of documentation, records, or forms that must be maintained to demonstrate compliance with this state rule.
attributes.references: State Recordkeeping Requirements

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the state compliance rule becomes legally enforceable and must be applied to staffing operations.
attributes.references: State Legislative Records

attributes.name: employer_size_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum number of employees or Full-Time Equivalents (FTE) that triggers applicability of this compliance rule. Null if applies to all employer sizes.
attributes.references: State Labor Law Employer Size Definitions

attributes.name: enforcement_agency
attributes.description: Name of the state or local government agency responsible for enforcing this compliance rule (e.g., California Labor Commissioner, New York Department of Labor).
attributes.references: State Government Agency Directory

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the state compliance rule ceases to be enforceable. Null for rules with no sunset provision.
attributes.references: State Legislative Records

attributes.name: ic_test_type
attributes.description: Type of legal test used by this jurisdiction to determine independent contractor classification (e.g., ABC test in California, common law test in other states). Only applicable for independent contractor classification rules.
attributes.value_regex: ABC test|common law test|hybrid test|not applicable
attributes.references: State Worker Classification Laws, IRS Revenue Ruling 87-41

attributes.name: jurisdiction_level
attributes.description: Geographic scope level of the compliance rule indicating whether it applies at state, county, city, or municipal level.
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) Jurisdictional Framework

attributes.name: jurisdiction_locality
attributes.description: City, county, or local jurisdiction name where this rule applies if more granular than state-level (e.g., San Francisco, Cook County). Null for state-wide rules.
attributes.references: U.S. Census Bureau Geographic Codes

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter state abbreviation where this compliance rule applies (e.g., CA, NY, TX).
attributes.references: ANSI INCITS 38:2009 (State Codes)

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this compliance rule was last reviewed by the compliance team to verify accuracy and currency.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Review Process

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this compliance rule to ensure it remains current with legislative changes.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Review Process

attributes.name: penalty_amount_max
attributes.description: Maximum monetary penalty amount in USD that may be assessed for violation of this compliance rule. Null if no maximum specified.
attributes.references: State Penalty Schedules

attributes.name: penalty_amount_min
attributes.description: Minimum monetary penalty amount in USD that may be assessed for violation of this compliance rule. Null if no minimum specified.
attributes.references: State Penalty Schedules

attributes.name: penalty_description
attributes.description: Description of penalties, fines, or sanctions that may be imposed for non-compliance with this state rule.
attributes.references: State Penalty Schedules

attributes.name: penalty_per_violation
attributes.description: Indicates whether penalties are assessed per individual violation (True) or as a single penalty regardless of violation count (False).
attributes.references: State Penalty Calculation Rules

attributes.name: posting_requirement
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance rule requires physical posting of notices at worksites or inclusion in job postings (True) or not (False).
attributes.references: State Workplace Posting Requirements

attributes.name: preempts_local_law
attributes.description: Indicates whether this state-level rule preempts or supersedes more restrictive local ordinances (True) or allows local jurisdictions to impose stricter requirements (False).
attributes.references: State Preemption Doctrine

attributes.name: regulatory_citation
attributes.description: Official legal citation to the statute, regulation, or ordinance that establishes this compliance requirement (e.g., California Labor Code Section 432.3).
attributes.references: State Legal Code References

attributes.name: requirement_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive description of what the compliance rule requires staffing operations to do or prohibits them from doing.
attributes.references: State Legislative Text

attributes.name: requirement_type
attributes.description: Category of state-specific compliance requirement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ban-the-box|pay transparency|salary history ban|state e-verify mandate|drug testing restriction|portable background check|paid sick leave mandate|predictive scheduling|wage theft prevention notice|state mini-WARN|independent contractor test variation|workers comp mandate|unemployment insurance requirement|disability insurance requirement|family leave mandate — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), State Labor Law Compendium

attributes.name: retention_period_years
attributes.description: Number of years that documentation related to this compliance rule must be retained. Null if no specific retention period mandated.
attributes.references: State Recordkeeping Requirements

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Internal risk rating assigned to this compliance rule based on penalty severity, enforcement frequency, and business impact of non-compliance.
attributes.references: Internal Risk Management Framework

attributes.name: rule_code
attributes.description: Business identifier for the state compliance rule, typically formatted as state abbreviation followed by rule category code (e.g., CA-BTB001 for California Ban-the-Box).
attributes.references: American Staffing Association (ASA) Compliance Framework

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the state compliance rule (e.g., California Ban-the-Box Law, New York Salary Transparency Act).
attributes.references: American Staffing Association (ASA) Compliance Framework

attributes.name: rule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the state compliance rule indicating whether it is currently enforceable.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Management Standard

attributes.name: source_url
attributes.description: Web URL link to the authoritative source document, legislative text, or regulatory guidance for this compliance rule.
attributes.references: State Government Web Standards

attributes.name: training_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance rule mandates specific training for recruiters, managers, or workers (True) or not (False).

products.name: placement_requirement_check
products.description: This association product represents the individual compliance requirement check results within a placement compliance gate-check process. Each record links one placement_compliance_check to one compliance_requirement and captures the specific check result, evidence, waiver status, and blocking determination for that requirement in the context of that placement. This is the operational record that compliance teams create, review, and manage to clear workers for assignment.. Existence Justification: In staffing compliance operations, each placement compliance gate-check evaluates the worker and placement against multiple compliance requirements (I-9, E-Verify, BGC, drug screen, credentials, safety training, client-specific mandates), and each compliance requirement is checked across thousands of placements. The business actively manages individual requirement check results with pass/fail/waived status, evidence references, waiver authorizations, and blocking determinations. This is not a derived correlation—it is the operational compliance checklist that humans create, review, approve, and use to block non-compliant placements from going active.

products.name: audit_finding
products.description: This association product represents the Finding relationship between compliance_audit and compliance_requirement. It captures each specific deficiency, gap, or non-compliance instance discovered during an audit that relates to a specific regulatory or contractual requirement. Each record links one compliance_audit to one compliance_requirement with attributes that describe the finding severity, remediation status, corrective actions, and evidence. Findings are actively managed business entities with their own lifecycle from identification through remediation to closure.. Existence Justification: In staffing compliance operations, audits systematically examine multiple regulatory and contractual requirements, and each requirement can be evaluated across many audits over time. Audit findings are actively managed business entities with their own lifecycle—compliance teams create finding records, assign owners, track remediation progress, manage corrective action plans, and report on finding trends. The business explicitly manages findings as distinct operational records, not as embedded attributes of audits.

products.name: violation_breach
products.description: This association product represents the breach relationship between a regulatory violation incident and the specific compliance requirements that were violated. Each record links one regulatory violation to one compliance requirement that was breached, capturing breach-specific attributes including severity assessment per requirement, financial penalty allocation per requirement, remediation status and timeline per requirement, affected population count per requirement, and breach narrative. Supports multi-requirement violation tracking, penalty allocation by requirement, remediation workflow per requirement, and regulatory reporting on repeat violations by requirement type.. Existence Justification: In staffing compliance operations, a single regulatory violation incident routinely breaches multiple compliance requirements simultaneously (e.g., an I-9 audit finding may violate federal I-9 completion requirements, state-specific verification requirements, and client-specific documentation mandates). Conversely, a specific compliance requirement (e.g., I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification) is violated across many separate incidents over time. The business actively manages this many-to-many relationship by tracking severity, penalties, remediation status, and affected populations per requirement within each violation, enabling requirement-level remediation workflows, penalty allocation, and regulatory reporting on repeat violations by requirement type.

attributes.references: Internal - M:N Association FK

attributes.name: requirement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific compliance requirement that was breached in this violation incident.
attributes.references: Internal - M:N Association FK

attributes.name: affected_population_per_requirement
attributes.description: Number of workers or clients affected by this specific requirement breach. A violation may affect different populations for different requirements (e.g., 50 workers for I-9 violations, 5 workers for OSHA violations in the same incident).

attributes.name: breach_date
attributes.description: The specific date on which this compliance requirement was breached within the context of this violation incident. May differ from the overall violation discovery date if the breach occurred earlier or if multiple requirements were breached at different times within the same incident.

attributes.name: breach_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing how this specific compliance requirement was violated within the incident. Provides requirement-specific context beyond the overall violation description.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this violation-requirement breach record was created in the compliance system.

attributes.name: penalty_amount_per_requirement
attributes.description: Monetary penalty amount allocated to this specific requirement breach. When a violation involves multiple requirements, the total penalty is allocated across the breached requirements. Enables penalty trending and risk assessment by requirement type.

attributes.description: Actual date on which remediation for this specific requirement breach was completed and verified. Used to calculate remediation cycle time by requirement type.

attributes.description: Current remediation status for this specific requirement breach. Enables tracking remediation progress per requirement when a violation involves multiple requirements with different remediation timelines and owners.

attributes.description: Indicates whether this specific requirement has been violated in previous incidents. Critical for regulatory reporting and risk assessment, as repeat violations typically carry higher penalties and regulatory scrutiny.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

products.name: state_credential_requirement

Existence Justification: In multi-state staffing operations, a single state compliance rule (e.g., California AB5 independent contractor classification) mandates multiple credentials (IC agreement, worker classification documentation, training certificates), and a single credential (e.g., OSHA 10 safety certification) satisfies requirements across multiple state rules (state-specific safety mandates, prevailing wage requirements, government contract rules). attributes.name: phone_number

attributes.name: postal_code

attributes.name: sic_code
